decisions.note: Round 1 scope table offered 'import existing browser bookmarks' as an alternative; client picked the no-import/export default, leaving both reference items unaddressed without ever weighing the tradeoff.

Spec (round 1) and MVP report (round 4) describe auto-collection of title only; reference requires title, description, favicon, and preview image on save — client approved both times without noting the narrower scope.

Round 4 explicitly states re-saving a duplicate url 'warns you (and lets you keep it anyway)'; reference requires re-save to converge to editing the existing bookmark, preventing duplicates outright. Client's 'that all works for me' passed over the contradiction.

Round 5 describes search as plain term-matching over title/url/note/tags; reference requires #tag syntax, AND/OR/NOT boolean operators with parentheses, and quoted-phrase exact match — none surfaced, client's approval didn't probe for them.
Round 5 describes tag entry as free-form comma-separated input with no autocomplete of existing tags, which the reference specifically calls for; client accepted the tag feature as presented.
